- NAT: control-plane uses source-preserving addressing when deployed in routed mode; we can optionally NAT to a fixed egress pool for customers that require single-IP allowlisting.
- Ports: we'll produce a one-page matrix (ports/protocol/purpose/direction) and a small CIDR suggestion for monitoring.

Thanks — dug into the attachments. I put together an initial control/data-plane matrix below and a short set of operational notes. Attaching as inline for quick review; I'll also drop a PDF to the Drive.

Control plane (recommended default)
- IP behavior: source-preserving by default. Optional egress-NAT pool: 198.51.100.0/28 (example pool we can reserve at cutover).
- Ports/protocols:
  - 443 TCP -> control API endpoint (mutual TLS), outbound from management VLAN to Redwood control endpoints (us-east-1.redwood.net:443)
  - 5222 TCP -> lightweight heartbeat channel (mTLS over persistent socket)
  - 16443 TCP -> k8s control-plane hooks (only when Kubernetes-based admin plane is enabled)
- Expected destinations: region-specific control endpoints (will provide final FQDNs).
- Observability: monitoring probes originate from the same control IPs; allow for active checks on port 9100/metrics as configured.

Data plane (tenant inference traffic)
- IP behavior: tenant IPs preserved; traffic should stay on tenant VLAN and not be NATed by default.
- Ports: 8000-8010 TCP (model inference); 9090 TCP (rpc/kv replication)
- Replication: KV replication between nodes uses ephemeral ports negotiated over the control channel; ensure ephemeral ranges are open between tenant pods and peer nodes within the colo pod.

Operational notes / risks
- Do NOT route control-plane over tenant egress — we saw session instability when control heartbeats traversed NATed tenant proxies in an earlier pilot.
- If Acme requires single-IP allowlisting, choose NAT option and we will publish the reserved egress pool 72 hours before cutover; expect small latency increase (~4–8ms).
- Certificate rotation: we rotate server certs every 30 days by default; rotation uses the control API on 443 and requires short-term connectivity to the Redwood CA endpoints.

Action items
- Logan: confirm whether Acme wants NAT egress pool reserved (yes/no) — required for security signoff.
- Jordan: will prepare a short runbook for cutover steps (BGP withdraw, route announce, ACL swap).
- Alice: share the final firewall ACL change window.

Kimberly Park
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
